minutes.headline: FinCom will likely fund an outside review of the school department's FY26 budget overruns from its reserve
minutes.summary: The Finance Committee got a preliminary, informational run-through of draft special town meeting warrant articles (zoning, stormwater fees, a veterans' exemption increase, PAC salaries, a $195,830 track/turf engineering request, and a special education reserve fund transfer) ahead of an October 8 discussion and October 22 public hearing for a November 17 special town meeting. The bulk of the meeting concerned a planned outside financial operations review of the school department's FY26 budget variance, to be funded from the Finance Committee's reserve account once a firm and scope are chosen; members also discussed possible tri-board meetings, a DLS workshop on financial policy, and committee reports on the municipal building project, the library, and the school finance director search.

budget_items.what_was_said: A planning board/stormwater task force article would create a fee structure for stormwater management, plus a non-binding straw-poll article asking the public to choose between funding stormwater/MS4 compliance through the operating budget or a utility.
The Board of Assessors intends to propose raising the veterans exemption from its current amount to either 600 or $800, with research still underway.
An article from the public access cable commission seeks a salary increase for the remainder of FY27, to be funded from retained earnings.

budget_items.topic: Track/turf field engineering, Lunenburg Middle High School
budget_items.what_was_said: The school committee submitted an article to fund engineering and bid-ready documents for reconstruction of the track and turf field; the overall project is expected to cost roughly $2 million, derived from a prior assessment.

budget_items.topic: Marshall Park special town meeting funding (precedent)
budget_items.what_was_said: A member noted Marshall Park was funded at special town meeting outside the normal capital planning process, as precedent for how the track/field project might proceed.

The school committee's draft article would transfer unexpended FY26 funds (once they roll into free cash) into the special education reserve fund to help offset unanticipated placement costs; no amount is available yet pending year-end closeout.

budget_items.topic: FY26 school financial operations review, funded from FinCom reserve
budget_items.what_was_said: A professional (non-audit) review of the school department's FY26 budget variance and financial practices is expected to be funded from the Finance Committee's reserve account; no price has been obtained yet from the firms being considered.

transfers.description: PAC salary funding from retained earnings account, pending town meeting authorization

decisions.decision: Warrant articles will get an in-depth discussion on October 8, a public hearing on October 22, ahead of a special town meeting planned for November 17.
The Finance Committee will likely fund a professional financial operations review of the school department from its reserve account once a firm, scope and price are settled.
The net school spending workshop item is tabled until the next meeting because the presenter is unavailable.

Whether to hold tri-board meetings, and on what topics (ambulance billing write-offs, an athletics department budget, free cash policy, school staffing strategy), is left to the three board chairs to work out; the finance committee vice chair will pass along member feedback.
The town manager and DLS will work out how a closed, non-deliberative financial-policy educational workshop can be scheduled without violating Open Meeting Law.
The finance committee vice chair will ask the current chair to bring a social media policy topic back to a future agenda.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee expects to fund an outside review of the school department's FY26 budget variance from its own reserve account.

Draft special town meeting articles got a first look -- stormwater fees, a veterans' exemption increase, PAC salaries, a track/turf field engineering request, and a special education reserve transfer.
Those articles move to an in-depth discussion October 8 and a public hearing October 22, ahead of a November 17 special town meeting.
A workshop on net school spending was tabled because the presenter could not attend.
Whether to hold joint tri-board meetings, on topics including an athletics budget and ambulance billing write-offs, was left to the three board chairs to work out.

why_it_matters: The planned review would look at why the school department's FY26 spending diverged from its budget, a question tied to special education placement costs.
The special education reserve transfer, the track/turf field funding, and a possible veterans' exemption increase would all go to voters at the November 17 special town meeting.
A new stormwater fee structure, discussed at this meeting, could show up as a separate charge on future bills depending on how the article is written.
